verdict.rationale: Convex has a CLI scaffold (`npm create convex@latest`) and a CLI that pushes code-defined schema and functions to a dev deployment. Authorization rules are written in function code, and the docs say agents can start new projects. That covers schema and policies as code deployed through the CLI. But the docs only describe a filesystem-watching dev loop, not non-interactive scripted provisioning, and auth setup is described as a library, not a CLI step. missing for 10: documented non-interactive/headless flags or deploy keys for scripted project and deployment creation, a CLI-driven auth provider setup step, a one-shot (non-watch) push command, and hands-on corroboration of an agent provisioning end-to-end in a script.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent stand up a new backend — schema, auth, and policies — headlessly from the CLI in a script

citations.quote: When you change a function or the schema, the new versions are pushed to your dev deployment and the generated types in convex/_generated are updated.
This architecture lets you check every public request against any authorization rules you can define in code.
you can implement auth directly in Convex with the Convex Auth library
Starting a new project is as easy as asking your agent to create a new app with Convex.
